# Calendar eligibility inspector fixtures

Run from the repository root (Node 24, no clock, browser or scheduler required):

```bash
node tools/learning/inspect-eligibility.ts tests/fixtures/learning/eligibility/late-night.json
```

Input version 1 contains the actual grading instant, unchanged raw scheduler due, explicit
scheduler phase/integer scheduled-day semantics, profile timezone and `HH:mm` boundary.
Review with `scheduledDays >= 1` uses calendar addition; all other results retain exact raw
due. Do not infer scheduled days by rounding an elapsed timestamp difference. The calendar
minimum elapsed gap defaults to six hours; `minimumGapHours: 0` explicitly disables it.
Optional injected `exposureEligibleAt`, `siblingEligibleAt` and `postponedUntil` gates are
already calculated by their owners; this inspector does not aggregate exposures/history.

Output separates actual/raw times, current/nominal/resolved target dates, each applicable gate,
the maximum eligibility instant and its controlling reasons. A window's suggested attendance
never changes eligibility. Windows are half-open; when eligibility is inside a window the
suggestion is eligibility itself. Midnight-crossing windows consider the previous day's tail.
Both endpoints use Temporal compatible resolution; collapsed/inverted windows are skipped.

Policy `calendar-v1-compatible-skip-empty` resolves each study-day boundary with T-003's
compatible adapter. If a target date's start equals its successor's start, it advances to the
first nonempty study day. After a skipped date, early-morning attempts belong to the last
nonempty day whose half-open interval contains them. Both the nominal target and resolved
target are reported; historical stored dates are never rewritten by this pure operation.

`cases.json` has literal expected instants, not expectations generated by the policy under test.
Calendar/gap UTC expectations were independently checked with Python's `zoneinfo` using the
fixture's IANA zone and boundary plus actual elapsed hours. Amsterdam's March/October changes
and Apia's December 2011 date skip are included, along with leap day and multi-day intervals.
Unit tests inspect all cases; CLI integration tests run the same files directly with Node.
T-003's one import now includes `.ts` so Node can resolve the reused adapter without a bundler.

Invalid versions, fractional/negative scheduled days, malformed instants/zones/times and
unknown fields fail without defaulting to the live clock or device zone. The eight-date search
bound is a fail-closed guard around timezone discontinuities, not an elapsed-day approximation.
No UI, preference persistence, clock anomaly logic or scheduler update is implemented here.
